title: Fast-path filtering and dynamic retention for real-time usage streams
creator: Aisha Karim
description:
Background:
We currently route all incoming console usage events through a single unified hot path that performs enrichment, normalization, and persistent write to the hot store. As volume grows for specific tenants (e.g., high-traffic demo accounts, long-running evaluation jobs), this creates sustained pressure on memory and CPU in the hot path and increases unit cost.

Goal:
Introduce a light-weight fast-path filter and per-tenant dynamic retention policy so that high-volume, low-signal event streams can be summarized or given short TTLs at ingress, while high-value events continue through the full enrichment pipeline. The feature should be configurable via the console control plane and support safe rollouts per-tenant.

Non-goals:
- Replace the existing enrichment pipeline.
- Implement a full re-ingest system for archived events (this ticket covers a minimal replay API).

Constraints and assumptions:
- Must not increase p95 write latency for non-filtered events by >10ms.
- Rules are evaluated at the ingestion proxy stage (closest to traffic source) to save downstream cycles.
- Per-tenant rules must be stored in the existing config service (with a cache) and be updatable without restart.

Proposed approach:
1) Ingress fast-path filter: lightweight WASM/Go plugin in the edge proxy that applies a small rule set (JSON rules) to decide: PASS -> full pipeline; SHORT_RETENTION -> write to hot-store with a tenant-specified TTL; SKIP -> drop after incrementing telemetry counters. Rules are limited to attribute checks (event.type, route, token tier, tenant labels) and simple rate thresholds.

2) Dynamic retention manager: control-plane API where PM/ops can set default and per-tenant retention policies. Policies include TTL windows (e.g., 30s, 5m, 1h), summary targets (e.g., sample 1/1000), and emergency throttle flags. The agent running on ingress nodes will cache policies and refresh via long-poll/stream.

3) Fast-buffer & small-window aggregation: for SHORT_RETENTION streams, keep a small in-memory ring buffer per tenant (configurable cap) to allow short replays for queries and to generate short-term rollups (counts, rate, percentiles). Downsampled rollups will be emitted to the warm path store every minute.

4) Safe rollout and override: enable a per-tenant "bypass" and an emergency override key for SRE to revert filtering quickly. Canary rollout will start with 5 pilot tenants (internal), then 20 beta tenants, then cluster-wide.

Observability and SLAs:
- New metrics: ingress_fastpath_decisions{pass,short_retention,skip}, fastpath_evaluation_ms (histogram), per-tenant_dropped_rate, short_retention_buffer_fill, short_retention_replay_success
- Alerts: per-cluster dropped_rate > 0.5% sustained over 5m for Production -> Page SRE.
- Cost target: reduce downstream hot-store ingest tokens by at least 12% on pilot tenants without increasing false-negative rate >0.5% on a labeled sample set.

Architecture references and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Fast-Path+Filtering+and+Dynamic+Retention
- Prototype PR (edge plugin + policy API): https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-proxy/pull/1289
- Simulation notebook + dataset (synth): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-simulations

Rollout plan:
- Week 1 (this ticket): implement plugin + local plugin tests + dynamic retention manager prototype (ingest config cache).
- Week 2: integration with hot-store TTL write path + buffer and rollup emitter + e2e tests with synthetic load.
- Week 3: internal pilot with 5 tenants; gather telemetry and tuning.
- Week 4: expand to beta tenants and begin production ramp with feature flag and SRE runbook.

Tradeoffs considered:
- Doing full enrichment at ingress would simplify correctness but increases cost. We favor a small rule surface to preserve signal for higher-value events.
- Placing policies in central DB + cache increases complexity but allows dynamic changes without restarts.

Open questions:
- What is the canonical schema for rules (we propose a 12-field JSON but PM to confirm)?
- Do we need deterministic sampling (seeded) for downstream correlation?

Next steps:
- Finalize rule schema with PM/design by 2025-03-05.
- Implement prototype of plugin and policy cache by 2025-03-12.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress plugin evaluates rules and emits decision metrics (pass/short_retention/skip) on synthetic traffic
Per-tenant retention policy can be set via control-plane API and is picked up by edge nodes within 60s
Short-retention writes include a TTL header honored by hot-store and evicted after TTL
Ring buffer per tenant supports short replay within TTL window and emits minute rollups to warm path
End-to-end tests show p95 write latency for PASS events increases by <10ms under target load
Pilot tenants show >=12% reduction in downstream hot-store token ingest without >0.5% false-negative loss on labeled sample
